board.name: Arduino Mega 2560

facts.v: ATmega16U2 (USB-B). Some clone boards use a CH340 chip instead; Linux has the driver built in.

Plug it in and run lsusb (Linux) or check Device Manager (Windows). USB ID 2341:0042 "Arduino Mega 2560 R3" means the ATmega16U2 chip, shown as /dev/ttyACM0 or a COM port. 1a86:7523 means a CH340 clone, shown as /dev/ttyUSB0.
20 mA per I/O pin, 50 mA from the 3.3V pin
256 KB flash (8 KB bootloader), 8 KB SRAM, 4 KB EEPROM

howToTell: An IOREF pin next to RESET on the power header (Rev3 only).
A second SDA/SCL pair next to AREF (Rev3 only).
A small chip marked 16U2 beside the USB socket (older boards had an 8U2).

components.name: 4-digit 7-segment display
components.blurb: Common cathode. The 4 digit pins are the cathodes and the 8 segment pins are the anodes. The kit sheet calls it 5641AS; the pinout is the same.

wiring.title: Direct wiring: 220Ω on the digit pins

notes: Front view: decimal points at the bottom, pin 1 bottom-left.
Common cathode: a segment pin HIGH lights the segment, and a digit pin LOW turns that digit on. Show one digit at a time (multiplexing).

Resistors on the digit pins only: a digit showing 8 looks dimmer than a 1, because its segments share one resistor. The Resistors box above lists the even-brightness options that stay under the 20 mA pin limit.
SevSeg: begin(COMMON_CATHODE, 4, digitPins, segmentPins, false). The last argument is false because the resistors are on the digit pins.
SevSeg gotcha: setNumber() only takes whole numbers. setNumber(22.82, 2) silently becomes 22 and shows 0.22. For decimals use setNumberF(22.82, 2).
A blank leftmost digit is normal for numbers under 10, because SevSeg hides leading zeros.

resistors.where: Each digit pin (12, 9, 8, 6), between the display and the Mega
resistors.why: The direct wiring above. Each digit draws at most about 14 mA, under the 20 mA pin limit. Digits with more segments lit look dimmer.

resistors.where: Even brightness, option 1: each segment pin (A–G, DP)
resistors.why: About 1.5 mA per segment, so a full "8." is 12 mA through the digit pin. Dimmer, but safe without transistors.

resistors.where: Even brightness, option 2: each segment pin, plus a PN2222 per digit
resistors.value: 8 × 220Ω on the segments, 4 × 1kΩ to the transistor bases
resistors.why: Bright and even. The transistors carry the digit current, so a digit pin HIGH turns that digit on.

components.name: 1-digit 7-segment display
components.blurb: Common cathode, with pins 3 and 8 as the shared cathode.
notes: For a common-anode version (5161BS), connect pins 3 and 8 to 5V instead, and invert the segment bits.

resistors.where: Each segment pin (A–G, DP), between the 74HC595 and the display
resistors.why: The 74HC595 can supply about 70 mA in total. With 330Ω, all 8 segments together stay under that.

components.name: LCD1602 character display
components.blurb: 16×2 characters, HD44780-compatible. Run in 4-bit mode it needs 6 Arduino pins.

rows.note: 220Ω in series (backlight; skip it if the module has its own)

notes: Code: LiquidCrystal lcd(7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12);
Blank screen or solid blocks? Turn the contrast pot.
Lessons 23 (thermometer) reuse this wiring.

resistors.why: Wiper to V0, ends to 5V and GND.

resistors.value: 220Ω if your module has no backlight resistor
resistors.why: Many LCD1602 boards have one on the back (often marked 101 or 151). If the backlight is very bright or hot, add one.

components.name: 8×8 LED matrix module
components.blurb: A MAX7219 driver drives all 64 LEDs over 3 data wires. Modules can be chained from DOUT to DIN.
notes: Code: LedControl lc = LedControl(12, 10, 11, 1); // DIN, CLK, CS, number of modules
The output header on the other end (VCC, GND, DOUT, CS, CLK) feeds the next module.
components.noResistor: The module has its own current-setting resistor.

components.name: Ultrasonic distance sensor
components.blurb: Measures 2–400 cm. A 10 µs pulse on Trig starts a reading, and the length of the Echo pulse gives the distance.
notes: Distance in cm ≈ echo time in µs ÷ 58.
components.noResistor: Connect it directly. Echo is a 5V signal, which the Mega accepts.

components.name: Temperature and humidity sensor
components.blurb: A single data wire carries both readings. The module has its own pull-up resistor.
notes: Read it at most once every 1–2 seconds. The kit sketch uses the non-blocking DHT library on pin 2.
components.noResistor: The module has a pull-up built in. A bare 4-pin DHT11 needs a 10kΩ from DATA to 5V.

components.name: Accelerometer + gyroscope
components.blurb: 6-axis motion sensor on I2C. Newer kits may ship a QMI8658C module instead (also covered in lesson 16).
notes: I2C address 0x68 with AD0 low (default), 0x69 with AD0 high.
The DS1307 clock module also uses 0x68. To use both, pull AD0 high on the GY-521.
components.noResistor: The module has I2C pull-up resistors built in.

components.name: PIR motion sensor
components.blurb: Output goes HIGH (3.3 V) when it sees motion. Two pots set the sensitivity and the hold time.
notes: Jumper H = repeatable trigger (motion keeps it high), L = single trigger.
Give it about a minute after power-up to settle.

components.name: Water level sensor
components.blurb: Exposed traces whose resistance drops as more of them is underwater. Read it as an analog value.
notes: The traces corrode when powered all the time. You can power + from a digital pin and switch it on only while reading.
components.noResistor: Connect it directly. The module has its own resistors.

components.name: Sound sensor
components.blurb: Microphone with an LM393 comparator. AO is the raw level; DO goes high past the threshold set by the blue pot.
components.noResistor: Connect it directly. The module has its own resistors.

components.name: Real-time clock
components.blurb: Keeps the time on a coin cell when the board is off. Talks I2C.
notes: I2C address 0x68, the same as the GY-521 by default.
The 2023 code download uses a DS3231 library for this lesson; the tutorial text describes the DS1307 module. The wiring is the same either way.
components.noResistor: The module has I2C pull-up resistors built in.

components.name: RFID reader
components.blurb: 13.56 MHz reader for the kit card and key fob. Uses the Mega's hardware SPI pins.
notes: Power it from 3.3V. 5V on the supply pin can damage the reader.
On an Uno the SPI pins are 10–13; on the Mega they are 50–53. Sketches written for an Uno need the pins changed.

links.label: MFRC522 library (pin table for each board)

resistors.where: Optional, for long-term use: SCK, MOSI and SDA lines
resistors.why: Brings the Mega's 5V signals down to about 3.3V. The kit lesson wires them directly.

components.name: Analog joystick
components.blurb: Two pots (X and Y) plus a push switch. About 512 at rest on each axis.
notes: The switch floats when not pressed, so use pinMode(2, INPUT_PULLUP). It reads LOW when pressed.
components.noResistor: None. Use INPUT_PULLUP for the switch.

components.name: 4×4 membrane keypad
components.blurb: 16 keys on 8 wires, as a matrix of 4 rows × 4 columns. Pin 1 is on the left with the keys facing you.
notes: Code: byte rowPins[4] = {9, 8, 7, 6}; byte colPins[4] = {5, 4, 3, 2};
components.noResistor: None. The Keypad library turns on the internal pull-ups.

components.name: IR receiver + remote
components.blurb: Decodes the 38 kHz signal from the kit remote. The output idles high and pulses low.
notes: IRremote 3 and later changed its API. Use the library version bundled with the kit if the lesson sketch will not compile.

components.name: Rotary encoder
components.blurb: Endless knob with a push switch. CLK and DT pulse out of step, and which one leads gives the direction.
notes: CLK is on pin 2 so attachInterrupt(0, …) catches every step.
components.noResistor: The module has pull-ups on CLK and DT. Use INPUT_PULLUP for SW.

components.name: Push buttons
components.blurb: The pins on each side are joined in pairs. Pressing the button connects the two pairs.
notes: With INPUT_PULLUP, a pressed button reads LOW.

resistors.why: The Mega's built-in pull-up (about 20–50kΩ) holds the pin HIGH. Without it, use a 10kΩ from the pin to GND.
Limits the LED to about 14 mA.

components.name: Tilt ball switch
components.blurb: A metal ball closes the contacts when the switch is upright.

resistors.why: The built-in pull-up holds the pin HIGH. Otherwise use a 10kΩ pull-up to 5V.

components.name: Servo motor
components.blurb: Turns to a 0–180° position set by a 50 Hz pulse.
notes: On the Mega the Servo library uses Timer5, so analogWrite() stops working on pins 44, 45 and 46 while a servo is attached.
More than one servo, or a servo under load, should run from the power supply module rather than the Mega's 5V.

components.name: Stepper motor + driver
components.blurb: 5V geared stepper, 2048 steps per turn of the output shaft. The ULN2003 board does the switching.
notes: Code: Stepper myStepper(2048, 8, 10, 9, 11); The order 8, 10, 9, 11 is deliberate. It puts the coils in the right firing order for this motor.
Keep the speed at or below about 15 rpm.
components.noResistor: Connect it directly. The ULN2003 board does the switching.

components.name: Motor driver chip
components.blurb: Dual H-bridge, 600 mA per channel. Drives the kit DC motor (lesson 29) and the relay coil (lesson 30).
notes: Pin 16 (VCC1) must be powered or the chip does nothing.
Notch on the left: pins 1–8 along the bottom, 9–16 back along the top.
components.noResistor: Connect it directly. Its outputs have clamp diodes built in.

components.name: 5V relay
components.blurb: A 5V coil switches a separate circuit. COM connects to NC at rest and to NO when the coil is energised.

rows.note: driven by the L293D, not straight from a pin

notes: The coil draws about 70 mA, more than a Mega pin can give (20 mA). Drive it through the L293D or a transistor with a flyback diode (1N4007).

resistors.where: Mega pin to the transistor base, if you drive the coil with a PN2222 instead of the L293D
resistors.value: 1kΩ, plus a 1N4007 diode across the coil
resistors.why: The diode soaks up the voltage spike when the coil switches off.

components.name: Shift register
components.blurb: Turns 3 Arduino pins into 8 outputs. Chain more chips from Q7' for more outputs.
notes: Pull the latch LOW, shiftOut() 8 bits, then pull the latch HIGH to update all 8 outputs at once.
Notch on the left: pins 1–8 along the bottom, 9–16 back along the top.

resistors.why: One per LED. The chip's 70 mA total limit means 330Ω is safer when all 8 are on.

components.name: RGB LED
components.blurb: Three LEDs in one package. The longest leg is the shared cathode.
notes: All three colour pins are on PWM pins so analogWrite() can mix colours.

resistors.why: One per colour, never one shared resistor on the common leg.

components.name: Buzzers
components.blurb: The active buzzer beeps at one pitch when given 5V. The passive one needs a tone() signal and can play notes.
notes: The active buzzer has a sealed back. The passive buzzer shows a green circuit board underneath.
tone() uses Timer2, so PWM on pins 9 and 10 is affected while it plays.

resistors.why: The lesson connects it directly. A 100Ω keeps the current comfortably under 20 mA.

components.name: Thermistor
components.blurb: Its resistance falls as it gets warmer. Pair it with a 10k resistor as a voltage divider.

rows.note: plus 10k resistor from A0 to GND

notes: B value 3950, 10kΩ at 25°C.

resistors.where: From A0 to GND (the other half of the divider)
resistors.why: Matches the thermistor's 10kΩ at 25°C, so the reading sits mid-range at room temperature.

components.name: Photoresistor
components.blurb: Its resistance drops in bright light. Read it through a voltage divider.

rows.note: plus 1k resistor from A0 to GND

resistors.where: From A0 to GND (the other half of the divider)
resistors.why: 1kΩ suits bright light. 10kΩ gives a wider range indoors.

components.name: Potentiometer
components.blurb: Outer legs to 5V and GND; the middle leg (wiper) gives 0–5V.
components.noResistor: None. It is a resistor itself.

components.name: Breadboard power supply
components.blurb: Plugs into both breadboard rails. It powers motors and servos so they don't load the Mega's regulator.

rows.note: connect its GND to the Mega GND

notes: 700 mA max. Line up the module's − pin with the blue breadboard rail.
If both jumpers are OFF, the LED and rails stay off.
